blocking.issue: The Node's fixed 128 MiB `totalBytes` cap contradicts the Configuration model's size rule. The Configuration model makes size limits configurable, proposes 64 MiB of source text and 20,000 resources, and promises that no Bundle that passes CI fails on a Node for size. A Snapshot carries the canonical form, in which every schema and registry default is materialized, and for large Bundles that can exceed the source size by a wide margin. An operator who raises the source limit also raises the snapshot size, but the Node's cap stays fixed. A Bundle that passes `ruralz bundle validate` and `build` can therefore produce a Revision that every Node NACKs deterministically with RZ-CFG-001, but only at Rollout time. The same size also fits the 256 MiB per-replica in-flight budget only twice. Neither Ruralz Control nor CI checks the encoded size before the Revision is recorded.
blocking.evidence: "Messages cap at 2 MiB (target); a `totalBytes` above 128 MiB (target) gets a deterministic NACK (RZ-CFG-001)." / "At most 32 concurrent Snapshots and 256 MiB in flight per replica (target)." vs Configuration model: "Size limits are configurable; exceeding one is RZ-CFG-001. The proposed defaults are 64 MiB of source text and 20,000 resources (target). A Node never enforces a limit below the CLI default, so no Bundle that passes CI fails on a Node for size."
blocking.fix: Make the encoded Revision size a build-time check. `ruralz bundle build` and the Ruralz Control builder reject, with RZ-CFG-001, any Revision whose Snapshot encoding exceeds the Node cap, so CI fails before merge and no Revision is recorded that Nodes would refuse. Derive the Node cap from the same configurable limit, never from a fixed value below the CLI default. Say that one Snapshot larger than the per-replica byte budget is admitted alone, not refused. If the Node cap needs a process setting or a field, add an Open question owned by configuration-model.

blocking.issue: The regional relay (Planned (M4)) has no way to receive the state it serves. Replica role 5 allows relays on 8092 only 'status forwarding and read-only content fetch'. Both classes carry data from the relay to the leader, or content fetched by digest. Neither carries committed metadata to the relay. Per-Node assignments, promotions with their sequences, revocations, anchor sets and `clusterNodeCount` are Raft metadata, not content objects, and a relay is not a Raft member. The fencing rule also defines staleness as having no word from a leader, but no class gives a relay leader contact. As written, the relay cannot learn what to send, cannot enforce revocations and cannot tell whether it is stale. This document decides OQ-system-overview-16 with this relay design, so the gap is in a decision it owns.
blocking.evidence: "8092 authorizes tagged classes by certificate role ... Raft and write forwarding only from current Raft members; status forwarding and content replication between replicas; status forwarding and read-only content fetch for relays" / "It receives committed assignments and revocations, caches content, forwards reports, enforces revocations and follows the [fencing rule]" / "A replica without word from a leader for one election timeout (hypothesis) is stale"
blocking.fix: Add an 8092 class 'relay feed', served by the leader or by a non-stale replica. It streams committed entries filtered to the relay's allowed Clusters: plan and assignment state with `storeEpoch` and `assignmentSeq`, signed promotions, revocations, anchor sets and `clusterNodeCount`. It resumes from the relay's last applied position, or sends a full state snapshot when that position is older than the retained log. It also carries the serving replica's last leader-contact time, so the relay's staleness is (time since the replica last heard from the leader) plus (time since the relay last heard from the replica), judged against the same election-timeout bound (hypothesis). Bound its queue and state what happens on overflow: resync. Add the class to replica role 5 and to OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15.

non_blocking.suggestion: A follower that still receives leader heartbeats but whose applied index is behind is not 'stale' under the fencing rule. It can send a reconnecting Node an assignment that the leader has since superseded, for example a batch assignment that a rollback overtook. The Node's fence accepts it because its sequence is higher than the Node's last activated one. The exposure lasts only as long as the replication lag, but that lag is unbounded while a snapshot installs. Define staleness also as applied index behind the leader's commit index by more than a bound, or make a follower send new configuration only after a read-index barrier.

Replica role 5 puts all 8092 classes under one 64 MiB/s per-peer cap. If Raft shares that cap, or a connection, with content replication, a large Revision can delay Raft heartbeats past the 1000 ms timeout and trigger needless elections. Say that each class uses its own connections and that the cap applies to content replication and relay feeds, never to Raft.

During a full quorum loss every replica is stale. With 'After 30 s stale (target) it sends Reconnect', every Node then reconnects repeatedly to other stale replicas for the whole outage. Send `Reconnect` only when a peer replica reports a leader, or at most once per stream.

Say where session state lives. The Raft rows of the data table list users, bindings and API token hashes but no sessions, and the memory row no longer lists them. The 30-minute idle timeout needs last-activity state that every replica can see. State one mechanism, for example session records written to Raft with the login audit entry plus a signed last-activity cookie that the serving replica refreshes, and add it to the data table.

'20 Snapshots/s (hypothesis)' needs a Snapshot size. At 50 MiB it means about 1 GB/s of egress per replica, and the 256 MiB budget allows five such Snapshots in flight. State the size behind the hypothesis, for example the median encoded Revision, and give the 5-minute batch target as a function of size.

Rotation step 2 re-signs 'each Cluster's assignment', but during a Rollout a Cluster has two live assignments: canary or batch Nodes on the new digest and the rest on the old one. Say that each distinct live assignment is re-signed at its own next sequence, or that rotation waits until no Rollout is active.

Audit batches go through Raft every 250 ms, and Raft entries must stay under 64 KiB (target). Say that a batch that would exceed the entry cap is split into several entries, so a burst of writes or logins cannot produce one oversized entry.

The ACK timeout starts at the last byte a follower writes. State that followers include that send time in status forwarding, and that Acks and Nacks received while the replica has no leader are buffered, bounded, until a leader returns.

ac_results.ac: The document states explicitly that Nodes keep serving their active Revision during a Ruralz Control outage and boot Last-Known-Good configuration after a restart, and lists what is unavailable during the outage.
ac_results.note: The Summary and 'Behavior during a Ruralz Control outage' state both rules, and a seven-row table lists what is unavailable. Stale replicas still serve Nodes without an active digest (L1-15 resolved).

ac_results.ac: Rolling back a Rollout takes three steps or fewer, shown as ruralz commands or Ruralz Console actions.
ac_results.note: 'Rolling back in three steps' shows three `ruralz rollout` commands and three Ruralz Console actions.

ac_results.ac: Control Stream contains a message table giving each message, its direction, key fields and ACK/NACK semantics, and covers enrollment, mTLS, snapshot plus delta, heartbeat and backpressure.
ac_results.note: A 12-row table has all four columns and includes the fence fields (`storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`, the signed promotion with `promotionSeq`, anchor-set `version`). Subsections cover Enrollment and mTLS, snapshot, delta and version skew, and heartbeat and backpressure. The size cap conflicts with the Configuration model (L1-17).

ac_results.ac: Ruralz Console lists at least eight screens in a table, with RBAC and SSO behavior.
ac_results.note: 12 screens with View and Act roles. 'RBAC and SSO' covers roles, separation of duties, PBKDF2 local accounts (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-21) and OIDC and SAML, Planned (M5).

ac_results.ac: Drift detection defines the reconciliation policy (what is detected, how it is reported, and when it is reverted or alerted).
ac_results.note: Four Drift kinds, each with a detection rule, how it is reported and a reconciliation action.

ac_results.ac: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle describes Revision signing by Ruralz Control and signature verification by Nodes, consistent with ADR-0017.
ac_results.note: The signing table covers content, keys, algorithm, Node verification, anchor sets and rotation, including re-signing and emergency removal (L1-6 resolved). It is consistent with pack 8.14. ADR-0017 is not written yet, and its adoption is tracked in OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24.

ac_results.ac: Rollout states match the foundation pack exactly: pending, canary, progressing, paused, complete, rolled-back, failed.
ac_results.note: The prose and Figure 3 use exactly the seven pack 8.3 states. Approval now happens before the Rollout exists (L1-9 resolved). The transitions to `failed` are proposed in OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15.

ac_results.ac: GitOps model covers repository layout, branch-to-Environment mapping, pull request validation and Ruralz Console write-back.
